type_data.full_teaching_text:
2- LunchBox: A powerful Plugin to generate panels and other functions.

Using the same referenced surface, let us check its flateness and visualize it with colors:

- Use the "Flatness Check" component from LunchBox Util Tab. 
- From the D OUTPUT, get the minimum and maximum of all values (using the "Bounds" component).
- Use the "Panel Frame" component from LunchBox Generate Tab in order to generate Panel Frames in relation to the Flateness Deviation Factor of each Panel.
This means that if a panel has a small D factor, it woud have a smaller opening that a panel with a bigger D factor.

- IMPORTANT!
If the difference between the minimum and maximum number of the D values is small, then you may need to REMAP all numbers with a new domain, to have a bigger bigger difference between the minimum and maximum (bounds of the values) so that the Panel Frame could be more perceivable.


- Visualizing Flatness Deviation:

- Get the "Gradient" component.
- L0 & L1: Need the minimum & maximum values of Deviation... For that, we need to deconstruct the domain in order to extract seperate values for minimum and maximum.
- Use the "Deconstrctu Domain" and extract the minimum and maximum values.
- Plug the minimum value into L0 and maximum value into L1.
- "t" INPUT represents the parameter along the gradient range.
We need to sort all values from minimum to maximum in order to assign the respective color range for each, according to its value order inside the list of values.
- Use the "Sort List":
- Feed all Deviation values into the K INPUT of "Sort List".
- Feed all the panels to be sorted into the A INPUT of "Sort List".
- The OUTPUT K & A of "Sort List" includes all panels sorted according to their Deviation values, from monimum to maximum.
- To visualize the colors, use a "Custom Preview" component:
- Feed the Gradient OUTPUT into S of "Custom Preview".
- Feed the sorted panels A into G of "Custom Preview.
- Now, we have an assigned color to each panel, following the gradient scheme, from least Deviation value to the greatest Deviation value.
